topic.title: Numeric Data Types and Operations
topic.description: Working with int, double, and other numeric types

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Numeric Data Types and Operations**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Working with int, double, and other numeric types
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Numeric Data Types and Operations** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
int a = 10, b = 3;
System.out.println(a + b);   // 13
System.out.println(a - b);   // 7
System.out.println(a * b);   // 30
System.out.println(a / b);   // 3 (integer division)
System.out.println(a % b);   // 1 (remainder)

double x = 10.0, y = 3.0;
System.out.println(x / y);   // 3.3333...

sections.title: Key Points
points: Java has six numeric types: byte (8-bit), short (16-bit), int (32-bit), long (64-bit), float (32-bit), double (64-bit)
Integer division truncates the decimal: 5 / 2 yields 2, not 2.5
The modulus operator % returns the remainder: 5 % 2 yields 1
Use double for decimal arithmetic; use int for whole-number counting and indexing
Arithmetic operators follow standard precedence: *, /, % are evaluated before +, -

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Numeric Data Types and Operations - Working with int, double, and other numeric types. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.
